subject.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing

question: Should a missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef degrade only during cold Gateway startup while remaining fatal for reload, restart-check, and config-write preflight?
rationale: Cold-start degradation preserves core availability, while uniform fail-fast behavior provides one simpler activation contract and earlier operator detection; source and tests cannot decide that product and operations tradeoff.

options.title: Approve cold-start degradation
options.body: Keep the current narrow scope, preserve strict later activation paths, and require exact-head lifecycle proof before merge.

options.title: Keep uniform fail-fast behavior
options.body: Remove the exception so unresolved active TTS SecretRefs abort every activation path consistently.

options.title: Design degraded status first
options.body: Pause the branch until status, doctor, or audit exposes a durable configured-unavailable state across lifecycle paths.

recommendation.title: Approve cold-start degradation
recommendation.body: Keep the current narrow scope, preserve strict later activation paths, and require exact-head lifecycle proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This cross-cutting Gateway availability versus SecretRef enforcement choice needs core product ownership.
